clue.text: Instruments right for singer to hold

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so the singer's word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a bass is a low-voiced male singer
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A vocalist is asked to carry the band's instruments to the right place.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside BASS to make BRASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is the collective name for trumpets, trombones, horns and similar wind instruments.

clue.text: Safari, perhaps, in south taken in by British sportsman

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for British

indicators.note: taken in by means received inside, so the compass point goes into the sportsman

parts.note: a rower is an oarsman
S is south

explanation.surface: A British athlete goes on an African trip in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Safari is Apple's web browser, not a wildlife trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Safari is an example of a web browser, the software used to view internet pages.

clue.text: Bulky piece found in middle of old embroidery

indicators.note: a piece from the middle means only the inner part is kept, the ends cut away

parts.note: a sampler is a traditional embroidered panel showing stitches

explanation.surface: A large fragment is discovered within some antique needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: SAMPLER loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means large or generously sized, as bulky does.

clue.text: Flashing light in bistro beckons

indicators.note: in signals that the word sits inside the next words of the clue

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A blinking light in a cafe invites customers inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe is a lamp producing rapid regular flashes, used in clubs and photography.

clue.text: It's good to greet fantastically dynamic figure

indicators.note: something done fantastically is wildly reimagined, so the following letters are reshaped

parts.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good
these seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An energetic salesperson is praised for greeting everyone with enormous enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good to greet' looks like one phrase, but only good is abbreviated; the anagram uses to greet alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-getter is an ambitious, energetic person who pursues success aggressively.

clue.text: Appeal to writer in sporting competition?

parts.note: O is the exclamation used in appeals and invocations, as in O Lord
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A plea is made to an author to take part in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as an example: the Open golf championship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Open is a tournament anyone qualified may enter, like the Open golf championship.

clue.text: Bank once on call in TV quiz show

parts.note: Egg was a British internet bank, now defunct
heads is a call when a coin is tossed

explanation.surface: A former bank is phoned during a television quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: Egg was a UK online bank. Eggheads is a BBC quiz where teams of champion quizzers face challengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggheads is a long-running British television quiz programme.

clue.text: Group of experts appropriate for an intellectual minefield?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a body that researches policy
second meaning: armoured vehicles cross minefields, so a mental minefield needs a vehicle for the mind

explanation.walkthrough: Tanks are used to cross minefields; for a minefield of ideas, a tank of the thinking kind is the joking fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A think tank is an institute of specialists researching and advising on policy.

clue.text: Agreement to go through field having missed a first set of marine races?

indicators.note: going through something means passing into it, so one piece sits inside the other
missing a first means an opening letter a is left out

parts.note: a field of study is an area
GATT was the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade

explanation.surface: A treaty is pushed through despite skipping some opening item.
explanation.walkthrough: AREA without its first A is REA; GATT goes through it: RE(GATT)A.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a sporting event of boat races, often on the sea or a river.

clue.text: Note in Pacific Island what's in the style of Latin American place

indicators.note: in places the note inside the island's name

parts.note: Guam is a US territory in the western Pacific
te is a note of the sol-fa scale
à la means in the style of

explanation.surface: A tone on a Pacific island is modelled on a Latin American country.
explanation.walkthrough: Guam is a US island territory in the Pacific; the French phrase à la gives the closing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Guatemala is a country in Central America, bordering Mexico.

clue.text: Suitable drink for consumption in old Indian city

parts.note: O is a common abbreviation for old

indicators.note: something taken in for consumption goes inside, so the drink sits within the city

parts.note: Pune is a city in Maharashtra, formerly Poona
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A beverage is deemed fitting to drink in a historic Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Pune is the modern spelling of Poona, a city near Mumbai; 'old' stays outside the container, at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune means well-timed or appropriate to the occasion, a close synonym of suitable.

clue.text: Composer showing sadness with shift in note finally

indicators.note: a shift is a change, so one letter of the word is swapped for another
finally points to the last position as the place where the swap happens

parts.note: grief is deep sorrow
G is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A composer's sorrowful mood is expressed by a change of key at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: GRIEF ends in F, itself a note; replacing that final F with G gives the Norwegian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Edvard Grieg was the Norwegian composer of the Peer Gynt music and the Piano Concerto in A minor.

clue.text: Basil perhaps tucking into prescribed iced food

indicators.note: tucking into something means burrowing inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: set means fixed or laid down, as prescribed
basil is an example of a herb, signalled by perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone named Basil eats a regulation frozen dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basil' poses as a man's name, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet, especially in American usage, is a frozen fruit dessert like a sorbet.

clue.text: Noted cleric and veteran Labour politician, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the name is matched by pronunciation not spelling

parts.note: Margaret Beckett, long-serving Labour MP and former Foreign Secretary

explanation.surface: A famous churchman and a long-serving Labour figure are compared.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Beckett's surname has two Ts; the archbishop's has one, but they sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Becket was the Archbishop of Canterbury murdered in his cathedral in 1170.

clue.text: Perhaps Venetian fruit is found in social engagement

parts.note: a Venetian blind is a type of window blind
the date is a palm fruit

explanation.surface: Fruit from Venice turns up at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venetian' suggests someone from Venice, but it is the slatted window blind.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind date is a romantic meeting between two people who have not met before.

clue.text: Flower moved from seat?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a thorny garden bloom
second meaning: stood up, past tense of a verb

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints at a flower being transplanted; instead the second half is simply getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a classic garden bloom and the past tense of rise, meaning got up from sitting.

clue.text: Alien figure in service abroad is withdrawn

indicators.note: in places the alien inside the reworked letters
abroad suggests being scattered far away, so the letters are dispersed

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
ET is the film's extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A foreign-looking person working overseas keeps to himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Secretive describes someone reserved and inclined to hide feelings, as withdrawn suggests.

clue.text: First person seen by a lord possibly and old woman in sensational performance

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several possible forms, so the letters can be arranged differently

parts.note: me is the first-person pronoun
these letters rearranged
old woman is slang for mother, MA

explanation.surface: A peer and his mother are watched putting on a showy theatrical act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' is informal for mother or wife; here it gives MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a play or show with exaggerated characters and sensational, emotional plotting.

clue.text: Like a good schoolboy, American, supporting film company

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece holds up the other from below, so it comes second

parts.note: a film studio is a production company
US means American

explanation.surface: A diligent pupil is backed by a Hollywood company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' sounds like backing a cause, but in a down clue it fixes the order of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Studious means diligent in study, the quality of a model pupil.

clue.text: Sporting event halted on ground around college

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the shuffled letters encircle the college
ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are reduced and reformed

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
C is a standard abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: An athletics competition was stopped on the field near a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' reads as the sports field, but it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: The decathlon is an athletics competition made up of ten track and field disciplines.

clue.text: Break up second airline engaged in racket close to fraud

indicators.note: engaged in means occupied within, so these pieces go inside the noise

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
S is the abbreviation for second
BA is British Airways

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: A rival airline is broken up after a fraud scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests a fraud scheme, but it is noise, DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To disband is to break up or dissolve a group or organisation.

clue.text: Oblique sun touching London suburb

parts.note: S abbreviates sun, as in Sunday
Kew is a district of south-west London, home of the botanic gardens

explanation.surface: Slanting sunlight falls across a leafy outer London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Skew describes something slanting or at an angle, which is what oblique means.

clue.text: Develop in detail gym session?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a phrasal verb, to plan thoroughly
second meaning: a session of exercise

explanation.walkthrough: As two words it is a verb for planning; as one it is a noun for exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out a plan is to develop it fully, and a workout is a bout of physical training.

clue.text: Distant station selector?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the handset used to change channels

explanation.walkthrough: 'station' suggests railways, but it is a TV or radio station.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote means far off, and a remote control switches between broadcast channels.

clue.text: Regular date arranged within borders of sanctuary

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are reordered
within means inside, so the shuffled letters sit between the edge letters
the borders of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A standing date is set up inside a peaceful refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular date' reads as one phrase meaning a partner, but only Regular is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady means constant and even, as a regular pace or pulse is.

clue.text: Wine and bit of grub stored aboard the German boat

indicators.note: goods stored aboard a vessel are inside it, so these pieces go inside the German article

parts.note: der is the German masculine definite article
red wine

indicators.note: a bit is a small part, here just the opening letter

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: Wine and food are loaded onto a German ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the German' is a common device for a German definite article, here the masculine form.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredger is a vessel that scoops mud and silt from the bottom of harbours and rivers.

clue.text: Open space in wood cheered leader of expedition

parts.note: cheered means made happy

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: Explorers' chief is heartened to find a clearing in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A glade is a clearing, an open area among trees in a forest.

clue.text: Ruffian hard to detect in towing vessel

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the vessel's name

parts.note: a tug tows larger ships
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A villain is difficult to spot aboard a tugboat.
explanation.definitionFit: A thug is a violent brute, the same kind of person as a ruffian.

clue.text: Friend getting a round to entertain fighter

indicators.note: to entertain is to host someone, taking them in, so the fighter goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
O is round in shape
a MiG is a Russian fighter jet

explanation.surface: A pal buys drinks for everyone to host a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a round of drinks; it is the letter O, which hosts MIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, widely used informally in English too.

clue.text: What Lancastrians might enjoy before small matter shortly becomes tricky issue?

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Lancashire hotpot is a lamb and potato stew
an atom is a tiny particle of matter

explanation.surface: A Lancashire meal before a minor matter turns into a thorny problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' places one piece ahead of the other. Lancashire hotpot is a slow-baked northern English stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a controversial issue that nobody wants to handle.

clue.text: Deck to get on in equestrian discipline

parts.note: to deck is to adorn or dress up
to get on is to grow older

explanation.surface: A rider dresses smartly to compete in horse events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' and 'get on' look like boarding a ship or mounting a horse; both are verbs of decorating and ageing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the Olympic horse-riding sport of precise trained movements.

clue.text: Seven triallists screened in the 400 metres?

indicators.note: something screened in is concealed behind a screen, so the word lies inside the phrase

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Seven athletes are watched competing in a track race.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the 400 metres as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The 400 metres is one race on an athletics programme, an example of a competition item.
